discovery: Photonic crystals: the photonic band gap and the control of light emission and propagation in periodic dielectric nanostructures
motivation: In 1987 Yablonovitch and John independently showed that a periodic dielectric can open a photonic band gap, a frequency range in which light cannot propagate. Yablonovitch proposed it as a way to suppress spontaneous emission; John showed it allows strong localization of light. This changed the electromagnetic vacuum from a fixed background into something that can be engineered. Yablonovitch then demonstrated the first full three-dimensional band gap. Noda turned the concept into rigorous experiment and practical devices: three-dimensional photonic crystals at optical wavelengths, ultrahigh-Q nanocavities, direct control of spontaneous emission, and photonic-crystal surface-emitting lasers that are now high-power, single-mode sources. Photonic crystals underpin slow light, cavity quantum electrodynamics with quantum dots, single-photon sources, nanolasers, photonic-crystal fibres and energy-efficient on-chip optical interconnects. Few concepts in modern optics have been as original or as productive, both for fundamental light–matter physics and for technology.
